Manage PCB design electromagnetic performance by controlling the impedance of every transmission line.
  • Impedance matching
    Manage and control the impedance for every critical signal throughout your board for an optimal high-speed design performance.
  • Signal insights
    Analyze your design signals to inspect parameters that characterize high speed design such as signal delays, trace length, impedance, inductance, and more.
  • Simple input parameters
    With simple input parameters and configuration, engineers can select signals of interest for quick analysis.
  • Make reliable products
    Ensure your High-Speed design capabilities meet the design specs and are compliant with industry standards.
  • Accelerate development cycle
    Improve your product development process by mitigating electromagnetic performance issues in the design phase.
  • Lower physical testing costs
    Minimize costly physical PCB testing and boards re-spins by virtualizing your design electromagnetic performance.

Attributes can be defined in the library (for individual devices), in the schematic or in the board. Attributes defined on the device level will be used for every part of that device type in the schematic. In a schematic, additional attributes can be defined for each part, and existing attributes from the devices can be overwritten with new values (if the attributes have been defined as variable). An element in the board has all the attributes of its corresponding part, and can have further attributes of its own.
The Load and Save options can be used to load the AutoRouter parameters from or save them to the given file. If filename doesn't have the extension '.ctl' it will be appended automatically.
Reusable bus specifications can be saved as Predefined Buses (PDBs). The PDBs are saved in a file and can be used across projects, even shared with others.

Circles in the layers RestrictTop, RestrictBottom, and RestrictVias define restricted areas. They should be defined with a width of 0.

ERC detects inconsistencies between the implicit power and supply pins in the schematic and the actual signal connections in the board. Such inconsistencies can occur if the supply pin configuration is modified after the board has been created.
The list view in the Errors dialog has up to four sections that contain Consistency errors, Errors, Warnings and Approved messages.

If a net wire is placed at a point where there are at least two other net wires and/or pins, a junction will automatically be placed.
Labels are handled as text, but their value corresponds to the name of the particular bus or net. If a bus or net is renamed with the Name command, all associated labels are renamed automatically.

When you select an airwire (a connection on the Unrouted layer), routing begins at the signal object connected to the airwire that is closest to your selection point. Otherwise, the Route Manual command automatically creates a new airwire from your selected route start point to a nearby target object that is a member of the same signal.
Left-click to place wire (double-click ends wire), Cmd/Ctrl right-click to change bends, Press SPACE to switch layers, '4' for SwapEnd or ENTER to complete the route.
Choose a grid fine enough before using the Mark command.

The meander starts at the first click point on the trace segment. For differential pairs, the target length matches the longest trace. Move the cursor along the trace to adjust meander's shape and length. Left click to place and add meander.
Tips
- Auto filled values can be overridden. - The default gap value is set by the Gap Factor, found in the Design Rules Editor.
Parts, pads, SMDs and pins can also be selected by their name, which is useful if the object is outside the current window area.

If you select a point where exactly two straight wires join, an additional wire will be inserted between these two wires, according to the given radius. If you click-drag on such a point with the left mouse button, you can define the mitering wire dynamically.
The orientation of the module instance can be defined textually using the definitions listed in the Add command, such as R0 or R90.
When moving elements, connected wires (tracks) that belong to a signal are moved too (beware of short circuits!).

Net wires snap to the tips of pins. When the mouse is within Snap_Length of any portion of a pin (either before or after grid snapping), a small circle appears at the tip of the pin. This indicates that if the mouse is clicked, the resulting net wire point will be placed at the pin tip, creating a connection to the pin.
When selecting a wire without name, all unnamed wires of the drawing are optimized.

Fill style is usually Solid, but the Hatched style can be used for a lower-capacitance fill.Thermals are On by default to provide electrical connectivity between pads and polygons while reducing thermal conductivity.
When pasting from a file, nets that have a label or are connected to a supply pin retain their names, while all others get newly generated names.

Wires attached to the swapped pins are moved with the pins, so short circuits can appear. Run the design rules check (DRC) and correct possible errors.

When the signal that you have selected is one side of a differential pair, the command automatically routes both differential pair signals together.

Select the traces to length tune. Click Tune Selected to automatically add meander.

Without parameters, the Replace command opens a dialog from which to select a device from all libraries currently in use. After such a device has been selected, subsequent mouse clicks on devices replaces those devices with the selected one if possible.
Useful when rerouting connections between components including memory signals, buses, etc
Use the Rotate dialog to select counterclockwise rotation angle ( 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees) and optional Mirror action (flip about Y axis).

When selecting an airwire of a differential pair, both signals are routed in parallel. The distance between the two signals as well as the wire and via sizes are determined by the signals' net class. This is done independent of the setting of Options/Set/Misc/Auto set route width and drill.

To select the signals to route, draw a selection line across the signal objects to be routed concurrently (existing wires, pads, and vias). Click to end the selection, then right-click to start the routing. Command line MINSPACING, INCSPACING, or DECSPACING for spacing.
Left-click to place wires, Cmd/Ctrl right-click to change bends, Press SPACE to switch layers, '1' for DecSpacing, '2' for IncSpacing, '3' for MinSpacing, '4' for SwapEnd or ENTER to complete the route.

A mouseclick defines the point at which the wire is split. The shorter of the two new segments follows the current wire bend rules and can therefore become two more segments; the longer segment is a straight segment running to the next end point.

Design reliable products with the Signal Integrity Extension
Manage PCB design electromagnetic performance by controlling the impedance of every critical transmission line.
Autodesk® Fusion® Signal Integrity Extension, powered by Ansys, enables designers to analyze PCB design electromagnetic performance, mitigate impedance mismatches and coupled geometries issues, to improve design performance and compliance, speed up development cycle, and lower physical testing costs.

The first click defines a point on a circle, the second its diameter. Right-click to change the direction from first to second point.
Positions selected objects in a linear or circular formation.
Select the objects to arrange. Specify the formation type, the X and Y spacing for rectangular or angular spacing for circular, and the start point. Click OK.
Definition of part attributes and their display.
An attribute is a combination of a name and a value that can specify any kind of information for a given part.

If signal names are specified or signals are selected with the mouse, only these signals are routed. Without parameters the command will try to route all signals. The command has support for general rules and custom rules with net class scopes.
Show or hide component origin markers on the bottom layer.
Draws buses on the bus layer of a schematic.

A Bus is a collection of nets. A Bus has a specification and is drawn as one or more bus line segments. The bus specification can include a unique alias, which is a short name used to identify the bus.
Breaks out a single, selected, or all nets as new wires extending from a bus.
Automatically add wires with net labels extending from a bus, saving time, and reducing errors.
The Change command is used to change or preset object properties. Select the desired parameter and value from the Change menu, or enter it from the keyboard.
Adds a circle to a drawing.
The Line Width parameter defines the width of the circle's line and is the same parameter used in the Line command.
Creates Net Classes and adds nets to them.
Net Classes are used by Design Rules and the Design Manager for scoping and organization of signals.
Provides presets to help configure which objects display in the 3D PCB document and whether or not bitmap images are used to represent traces.

Select the 2D PCB objects you want represented in the 3D PCB document. Components without a 3D model are identified so you can decide whether or not to exclude them. Included components without 3D models are represented by rectangular shapes.
Makes all hidden PCB sketches visible.

Copies objects within the same drawing, or between libraries. The system generates a new name for the copy but retains the old value. When copying signals (wires), buses, and nets the names are retained, but in all other cases a new name is assigned.
Transfers selected properties of an object to other objects of the same type.
Select the properties you want to transfer to other objects of the same type in the Select properties dialog of the selected object, then close the dialog with OK, and click the target objects.
Design rules are evaluated each time rules are checked. Can load design rule presets from external sources and scope design rules to defined parameters.

Parts, pads, SMDs, pins and gates can also be selected by their name, which is especially useful if the object is outside the currently shown window area. Note that when selecting a multi-gate part in a schematic by name, you will need to enter the full instance name, consisting of part and gate name.
Edits parameters that drive design geometry.
Preferences include Layer Stack, Annular Ring, Pad/SMD Shapes, Thermal Isolation, and Masks. Adjusting these settings automatically calculates PCB geometries according to preferences.

If an object is first selected, a dimension is applied, such as the length of a straight wire, or diameter of a hole. If no object is selected, the current dimension type is added; right-click to cycle through the various types.
Control the display of drawing layers, showing all, used layers, or unused layers.
Use the eye icon beside a layer to turn it on or off. Double-click a layer to review or modify its properties.
Add, modify, or delete document-level attributes, such as author or project identification number. Use the Text command to place the attribute string in the canvas.
Use this command to test schematics for electrical errors. If a board file is loaded, the ERC command also runs a consistency check between schematic and board.
Edits the 3D model associated with a part or element in a schematic or board.
When a custom 3D model is associated, edits the custom 3D model instead of the originally managed 3D model.
Edits the primary sketch that defines the board outline.
Create a closed profile to define the board. You can project geometry from the assembly context to ensure the PCB outline stays updated with the mechanical assembly.
Errors, if detected, are displayed in the Errors panel. Real-time rule checking can be enabled in the application settings for instant error detection.
Exports libraries to allow you to make individual changes to components in a project.
Use to generate one or more libraries containing the selected components. Make your changes in the libraries and then use UPDATE to display the changes in the schematic or board.
Creates fanouts from devices and signals.

The command creates a routed wire and attached via from pads of the selected device or signal. Only surface mount devices (SMD) or ball-grid array (BGA) devices are fanned out; devices with through-hole pads are ignored.
Rotates components and objects along their X-axis and places them on the opposite side of a double-sided PCB.
Choose to reroute, disconnect, or unroute the electrical connections.
The board is rotated 180 degrees around the Y axis, in model space, to look at the opposite side.
Swaps equivalent gates on a schematic.
Both gates must be identical with the same number of pins and the same Swaplevel in the device definition, but they need not be in the same device.
Provides controls for defining the drawing grid.
Set grid display on/off, display style, and size.
Enable to synchronize selections across schematic and 2D PCB. Selecting an item in one view automatically selects the corresponding item in the other.
Selection is always active and the active selection mode displays here.

Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Change the active selection mode by selecting the mode you want to work with from the menu. Use the selection mode and selection filters to fine tune selection.
Selects objects enclosed in a polygon selection area.
A clockwise boundary shape selects all objects within the boundary. A counterclockwise boundary shape selects all visible objects crossed by the boundary.
Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.
Selects objects enclosed in a rectangular selection area.

Click and drag from upper-left to lower-right (window selection) to select objects enclosed by the selection boundary. Click and drag from lower-right to upper-left (crossing selection) to select all visible objects the selection boundary intersects and encloses.
Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.
Ignores design rules, allowing different copper objects to connect.
An object's properties are displayed in a dialog, where they can be modified.
Inserts a previously saved 2D PCB in the canvas of the active 2D PCB.
Inserts a previously saved design block (.dbl) in the canvas of the active 2D PCB.
If a schematic is associated with the inserted design block a new sheet containing the schematic is added. Switch to the Schematic to view the sheet.
Inserts a previously saved design block (.dbl) in the canvas of the active Schematic.
If a 2D PCB is associated with the inserted design block the components are positioned at the bottom left of the PCB. Switch to the 2D PCB to reposition the components.
Browse to and select a DXF or DWG file.
Specify the desired insert values. To explicitly place the file, use Placement Origin. To implicitly place the file, click the location in the canvas.
Select the file, specify the insert values, and click in the canvas to place the file, then click Done.
Inserts a previously saved project in the canvas of the active 2D PCB.
If a schematic is associated with the inserted project a new sheet containing the schematic is added. Switch to the Schematic to view the sheet.
Inserts a previously saved project in the canvas of the active Schematic.
If a 2D PCB is associated with the inserted project the components are positioned at the bottom left of the PCB. Switch to the 2D PCB to reposition the components.
Inserts a previously saved schematic in the canvas of the active Schematic.
Browse to and select an SVG file.
Specify the desired insert values. To explicitly place the file, use Placement Origin. To implicitly place the file, click the location in the canvas.

Choose the Target Layer to place the vector image. When checked, Strokes Only will not fill any of the strokes from the vector image. Group will create a persistent group findable in the Design Manager. Scale factor will adjust the size of the placed image relative to original image dimensions.

To move vector image as a whole, first select Group from Design Manager or draw a selection window around all curves on canvas.

If vector image does not import correctly, try simplifying image by reducing to one single color and removing background shapes.
Calls a specific symbol from a device.
Select a particular gate from a device already in use and place it in the schematic (example: a power symbol with Addlevel = Request).
Places a dot at intersecting nets.

A connection dot is placed at the intersection of nets to be connected. Junctions can be placed only on nets. If placed on the intersection of different nets, the user is given the option to connect the nets.
Attaches text labels to buses and nets.

Bus or net names can be placed on a schematic in any location. Click the bus or net with the mouse, and the relevant label attaches to the mouse cursor. It can be rotated (right click), and moved to a different location or layer. The second mouse click defines the location of the label.
Use the Schematic or PCB Display command to review and modify the layer display.
Switch to the previous available layer.
Cycles through layers in reverse sequence order, skipping hidden or unavailable layers.
Switch to the next available layer.
Cycles through layers in sequence order, skipping hidden or unavailable layers.
Directly navigates to the Layer Stack page, making it easier to manage and adjust board layer composition.

The line begins at the first point specified and runs to the second. Additional points draw additional line segments. Two mouse clicks at the same position finish the line, and a new one can be started at the position of the next mouse click.
Converts unrouted connections into routed wires (tracks).
This command activates the manual router, which converts airwires (unrouted connections) into real wires.
Defines a mark on the drawing area.

The X and Y coordinates of the mouse cursor relative to that point are displayed above the canvas, with an R prefix, polar coordinates with P prefix. This command is useful when defining locations of components or cutouts. Enter MARK; to turn the mark off.
Length tunes the length of a single trace or differential pair by adding a meander.
Rotates symbols, objects, and text along their Y-axis and repositions them as a mirror of the original placement.
Use Mirror to simplify the design while you avoid crossing nets.
Use this command to take the edge off a point where two wires join. The two wires must be on the the same layer, and must have the same width and wire style.
Creates a module, and adds it to a new sheet.

Parts, pads, SMDs, pins and gates can also be selected by their name, which is especially useful if the object is outside the current window area. Note that when selecting a multi-gate part in a schematic by name, you will need to enter the full instance name, consisting of part and gate name.

Parts, elements, pads, SMDs, pins and gates can also be selected by their name, which is especially useful if the object is outside the currently shown window area. Other object types (e.g. nets, buses, signals) have to be clicked first.
Draw nets and mark pins as No Connection (NC) on a schematic.

Draw individual connections (nets) on the Net layer of a schematic drawing. Click once to start a net and again to end a segment. Double-click the same point to finish the net. Or, mark pins as No Connection (NC).
Breaks out nets from any pin of a component in the schematic.
Automatically add wires with nets assigned to devices like microcontrollers and RAM, to save time and reduce net connectivity errors. You can use auto-increment and custom label formatting options.
Displays custom net class and signal colors to make them easier to differentiate.
Press %1% to show or hide colors in the canvas.
Customize appearance in the Inspector or Properties panel.
Makes multiple instances of the selected object(s) and places them in a linear or circular formation.

Select the objects to pattern. Specify the number of instances in the pattern, the X and Y spacing for rectangular, or angular spacing for circular patterns, and the start point for the pattern. Click OK .

This command joins wire segments that lie in a straight line. The individual segments must be on the same layer and have the same width. This command is useful to reduce the number of objects in a drawing and to facilitate moving a complete track instead of individual segments.
Polygon cutout on a routing layer will produce a void area in a polygon pour.
Polygons are used to create a copper sheet or layer for a signal, and must reside on a routing layer.
Polygon is a simple non-signal solid polygon shape on any layer.
Adds a package to the component.
This command attaches a package to the component to create a variant.
Opens a dialog to search for packages from library.io.
This command attaches a package to the component to create a variant.
Adds Plated Through-Hole (PTH) pads on a footprint.
PTH Pad dialog adjusts pad properties such as Rotate, PadShape, and Dimensions. Pads can be placed in the footprint area and are named sequentially based on their placement.
Adds a series of PTH pads on a footprint.

Enter a Base Name, pick pad sides, select a shape, set pad numbers and start index. Add a border with >NAME and >VALUE labels and adjusts pad spacing in X and Y directions. Selecting OK places the pads.
Attaches a copy of the clipboard contents to the cursor, left click places the content at the cursor location on the specified layer.

Use Group, Copy, Cut, and Paste to add or subtract elements to or from your design, design block, or library component. Use right click to rotate the contents, in 90 degree increments, before placing it.
Creates pins using data copied to the clipboard from an external source.
Copy pin data from a datasheet, spreadsheet, or text file and then paste it into the current document.
Show or hide component origin markers on PCB.
Adds a Pin into an integrated circuit (IC) or chip symbol.
Pins on symbols establish the connectivity. Each pin can have unique properties during placement.
Adds a series of Pins into an IC or chip symbol.

Pin Arrays establish connectivity on symbols. Arrays can be personalized with a Base Name, selected placement sides, and distinct pin numbers and starting index. Including a rectangular outline and >NAME and >VALUE labels are optional.
Breaks out all or a selection of pins from the part by extending nets a short distance from the pins.
New nets connected to pins are drawn and can be automatically named and labeled.

Use this command to swap pins within the same symbol that have the same swaplevel (> 0). If a board is tied to a schematic via Back Annotation, two pads can only be swapped if the related pins are swappable.
Hide fill for all polygon pours.
Polygon pours are represented by an outline.
Doing this repairs any damage to polygon pours as a result of moving components or cutouts.
Show fill for all polygon pours.
Restore the fills for polygon pours after they were hidden.
Use this command to add ports to modules used in hierarchical schematics.
Moves existing copper objects to make way for new copper objects while maintaining connectivity.
In QuickRoute Airwire mode, you select individual airwires to be automatically routed, and they are instantly routed according to design rules.
Automatically routes multiple signals along a sketched path.

Draw a selection line that intersects the signal objects you want to route concurrently (existing wires, pads, and vias). Right-click and draw the path for the selected signals. The signals are routed on the active layer with the fewest wire bends.

Draw a selection line that intersects the signal objects that you want to route concurrently (existing wires, pads, and vias). Continue to draw additional selection lines to add more signal objects. Right-click to route all the airwires connected to the selected objects. The signals are routed on the active layer.
Automatically routes a group of signal segments with the same name.
Select any signal object (airwire, wire, pad, or via) and the command instantly routes all airwires that are members of that signal.
Automatically smooths the wire sequence on a selected signal.
QuickRoute Smooth reduces the number of wire bends and segments in the sequence.
Automatically tunes the length of multiple traces, differential pairs, or busses by adding meanders.
Two points define two diagonally opposite corners of the rectangle.
Removes a custom 3D model override from an element or part.
The originally assigned 3D model reference is restored when you remove the override.
Renumbers selected reference names based on preset options.
The table will preview the proposed updates.

Use this command to replace a schematic component with a different component (even from a different library). The old and new device must be compatible, in that their used gates and connected pins/pads must match, either by their names or their coordinates.
Reverrts all routed wires and vias to airwires, and changes the display of polygons to outlines.
This is usually done to prepare for re-routing all signals.
Ripup Connected rips up 'direct' connections along a signal path.
Use this command to limit the scope of a ripup and make reworking sections easier.
The entire trace is reverted to airwires.
Use to ripup all tracks, vias and polygons in a selected signal
Use this command to change the orientation of objects.
Converts unrouted connections of a differential pair into routed wires (tracks).

This command activates the differential-pair manual router, and the differential pairs in the design are highlighted. To begin routing a differential pair, click one of the highlighted differential pair airwire or copper objects.
Converts multiple unrouted connections into routed wires (tracks).
This command activates the manual router, which converts multiple airwires (unrouted connections) into real wires.
Executes the commands in a script file.
Use this command to execute sequences of commands that are stored in a script file.
Show or hide component origin markers in the schematic.

Highlight complete signals and nets with the Show command. Select parts in Design Manager or enter names on the command line in format @ <partname> (example: @ FB2 FB4). If a bus is selected, all nets belonging to that bus are also highlighted.
Rips up short trace segments or longer segments to left or right.
Separate multiple board traces or schematic nets for rerouting. The width defines how much of the line is ripped up by the slice. Left or right options can be selected to rip up longer segments.
Adds Surface Mount Device (SMD) pads on a footprint.
SMD Pad dialog adjusts pad properties such as Angle, Size, and Roundness. Pads can be placed in the footprint area and are named sequentially based on their placement.
Adds a series of SMD pads on a footprint.

Enter a Base Name, pick pad sides, select a shape, set pad numbers and start index. Add a border with >NAME and >VALUE labels and adjusts pad spacing in X and Y directions. Selecting OK places the pads.
Splits wires and polygon edges, adding new segments.
Split a wire, segment, or polygon edge into two segments in order, for example, to introduce a bend. Split wires into parts that can be moved with the mouse during the Split command.
Adds Via Stitching to a board.
Adjust settings like offset, spacing, pattern, and via sizes. Click OK to apply Via Stitching. Draw a Polygon to target a specific area, if not covering the entire board.
This command will toggle a panel that can be used to place components onto a schematic, or footprints onto a board.
Moves vias to accommodate new copper objects.
Switches betwen displaying all board layers and only the active layer.
Useful when routing a dense design.
Show or hide component origin markers on the top layer.
Converts routed wires and vias into unrouted signals, and changes polygons to outlines.
Choose an unroute method to control which wires are affected.
Converts all wire segments and vias to unrouted signals.
Converts all stubs and incomplete segments to unrouted signals.
Assign values to circuit elements, such as '1k' for a resistor.
When the Via command is active, a via symbol is attached to the cursor. Click to place a via at the current position.
Manages interactions between copper objects, including traced routes and vias, based on preferred clearance in Design Rules.
Moves new copper objects around existing copper objects and components while following Design Rules.
Syncs changes from 2D PCB to 3D PCB. If no 3D PCB is linked, creates a new 3D PCB document. Provides preferences for object visibility and fidelity in the 3D PCB document.
Select the 2D PCB objects you want in the 3D PCB. Components without 3D models are identified and represented by rectangular shapes if you include them.
Creates a 2D PCB document for the active Electronic design.
Schematic and 2D PCB documents are automatically synchronized. For design efficiency, create the schematic first then the PCB. Useful for creating 2D PCB designs that do not require a schematic.
Create the PCB, the components in the schematic are placed at the lower left. Position them according to your design needs.
Creates an empty schematic document for the active Electronic design.
Only one schematic is used for each design. A schematic can have as many sheets as are needed, up to 999, for designing the board diagram.
This is the starting point of the new design. Create the schematic, then the PCB layout of the components in the schematic.
Syncs changes from 3D PCB to 2D PCB. If no 2D PCB is linked to 3D PCB, creates a new 2D PCB document.
Once you link a 2D PCB, you can remove the link only in 2D PCB.
Adds a non-plated through hole to the 3D PCB. When synced to 2D PCB, generates a symbol on the Holes layer and a circle with the diameter of the hole on the Board Outline Layer.
Select a hole type, select a face or sketch point to place the hole, and specify the hole diameter. For At Point type, select references for precise hole positioning.
Links an existing PCB document to this 3D PCB. Only one 2D PCB can be linked at a time.
To link a different 2D PCB to this 3D PCB, remove the link from the 2D PCB.
Links an existing PCB document to the active Electronic design.
The referenced PCB document is added to the design. Changes to the referenced PCB also change this design PCB.
Doing this helps preserve synchronization between project documents and improves management.
Links an existing schematic document to the active Electronic design.
The referenced schematic displays in the Sheets section of the Schematic document. Changes to the referenced schematic also change this design schematic.
Doing this helps preserve synchronization between project documents and improves management.
Switches to a 3D Model of the 2D PCB that can be inserted into a mechanical assembly. If no 3D PCB exists, creates 3D PCB.
Switches to a 2D layout of the physical printed circuit board that defines component placement and routing. If no 2D PCB exists, creates 2D PCB.
Switches to a logical representation of the electronic circuit that defines signals and connections.
Unavailable when another user has the Electronics Design Reserved.

Unavailable when another user has the Electronics Design Reserved.
Syncs changes from 2D PCB to 3D PCB. If no 3D PCB is linked, creates a new 3D PCB document. Provides preferences for object visibility and fidelity in the 3D PCB document.

Components without a symbol cannot be placed in the schematic.
